Hadhrat Umar (RA) Fixes an Allowance from the State Treasury for an Old Dhimmi

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abi Hadrad Aslami (RA)
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abi Hadrad Aslami (RA) narrates that when they arrived with Hadhrat Umar (RA) in Jaabiya, they came across an old Dhimmi man begging for food. When Hadhrat Umar (RA) enquired about the man, he was informed that the man was a Dhimmi who had grown very old and weak and even had a family to support. Hadhrat Umar (RA) then absolved him of paying the Jizya he was obliged to pay and said, "You have made him pay the Jizya and when he eventually became weak, you left him to beg for food?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) then fixed an allowance of ten Dirhams for the man from the state treasury. [^2]

Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed by an old Dhimmi begging at the doors of the Masaajid. Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "We have not treated you fairly. We had been taking Jizya from you when you were young and now that you are old, we have not cared for you." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then had an allowance given to him from the public treasury that was adequate for him. [^3]
The Incident of Hadhrat Umar (RA) and a Dhimmi

Hadhrat Yazeed bin Abi Maalik reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was with the Muslims of Jaabiya when a Dhimmi reported to him that people had ransacked his vineyard. Hadhrat Umar (RA) went to investigate and even found one of the Sahabah (RA) carrying a shield full of grapes. "You also?" gaped Hadhrat Umar (RA). The Sahabi (RA) said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! We are starving." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then left him and gave instructions that the owner of the vineyard should be paid (from the state treasury) for his grapes. [^4]
